## Summary
Lenses checked: correctness, silent-failure, tests, comments.
`Cache.set` stores keys without lower-casing them, so `get` cannot find any value set under a mixed-case key. Fix this before merging.

## Changes
The pull request adds a `Cache.set` method and raises `Cache.DEFAULT_TTL` from 60 to 300 seconds, with the comment updated to match. It also adds tests for the set/get round trip, the default TTL value and expiry.

## Critical
- app/cache.py:27 — correctness — Lower-case the key in Cache.set — `c.set("Alpha", 1)` stores the value under `"Alpha"`, but `c.get("Alpha")` looks up `"alpha"` and returns `None`. This breaks the rule at `app/cache.py:14`: "every path into _store lower-cases the key first". — Values set under mixed-case keys can never be read and are never removed from `_store`. — Fix: write `self._store[key.lower()] = ...`, and change `test_set_then_get_round_trip` to call `set` with a mixed-case key.
